I've been a Smash Bros player for a very long time (I'm only average with fighting games so I barely have any experience with other games like Street Fighter for example) & I was curious what the /v/gaming community recommends because like MMOs I've avoided fighting games like the plague but I've decided to try to get serious with them.

The only recent games that I personally enjoyed was Pokken Tournament (I'm not a pokemon fan) & the Soul Calibur series (except for the 5th game).

The only rule I have is that I'm looking for a fighting game with combos that aren't too short and not too long + easy, responsive controls.

I got a few recommendations from steam users in a group chat telling me to try out Guilty Gear Xrd Revelator, Dead or Alive (I tried the 4th game and I hated the AI + I don't plan on renewing my Xbox Gold) & King of Fighters 98 + 2002.
What fighting games would you recommend to someone that has barely touched the genre?
Guilty Gear is great, and so is Tekken
If you are going to do street fighter, then the best one by far is Street Fighter Alpha 3
Super Smash Brothers, the newer ones have an easier learning curve, but Melee and Project M are the best.

Steam is totally right on KOF 98 and 2002. They aren't incredibly complicated but both so good. Easy to learn, hard to master sort of games. You might prefer 98 more because 2002 is more combo heavy.

If you end up wanting to get into retro fighters, consider downloading Fightcade. It emulates your totally legally acquired ROMs and you can play online or offline. Or just buy them. Good way to demo them though.

Killer Instinct is very fun, free to play, and doesn't have a high learning curve, it's definitely one of my favorites.

Also has insane combos that aren't difficult to pull off.

If you want something simple, then there are two games: Nidhogg and Divekick.

Divekick has only two buttons and the game is based off the divekick move present in fighting games. Despite its simplicity, it still has the tension and strategy you need.

Nidhogg has a bit more complex moveset even though it only has functionally 1 character. However, while the game is easy to pick up, it's hard to master.
